'''''Prey''''' is a 2017 [[first-person shooter]] [[immersive sim]] video game developed by [[Arkane Austin]] and published by [[Bethesda Softworks]]. It occurs in an [[alternate timeline]] in which mankind has taken to orbital stations following an accelerated [[Space Race]]. The player plays as Morgan Yu, a member of a scientific team aboard the space station ''Talos I'' researching the Typhon, a hostile alien force with both physical and psychic powers. As the Typhon escapes confinement, the player uses various weapons and abilities to survive, progressing to end the alien outbreak and ultimately escape ''Talos I''. The player gradually gains access to areas of ''Talos I'' through linear mission progression until they can explore the station freely, acquiring key items and abilities along the way. 

Development of the game started after Arkane Austin completed its work on ''[[Dishonored]]'' (2012). [[Raphaël Colantonio]] served as the title's director. Arkane's ''Prey'' is largely unrelated to the 2006 game ''[[Prey (2006 video game)|Prey]]'' or [[Prey 2|its cancelled sequel]]. It did not use any of the planned sequel's assets and only incorporated the previous game's name and the broad theme of the protagonist being hunted by aliens. Arkane built ''Prey'' as a [[spiritual successor]] to ''[[System Shock]]'' (1994), giving players multiple avenues to approach and tackle missions while considering the ''Talos I'' station a thematic reinterpretation of the underground dungeon from their debut game, ''[[Arx Fatalis]]'' (2002). The game combines elements of first-person shooters, [[role-playing video game]]s, [[stealth game]]s, and [[Metroidvania]]s in its design. Aliens in the game were designed to be enigmatic, with their design being inspired by paranormal elements rather than stereotypical insect- or lizard-like species.

The game was released for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox One]] on May 5, 2017. It received positive reviews from critics, who praised the game's setting, level design, environmental storytelling, and themes, though its main story and gameplay received a mixed response. The game's reputation improved over time. Retrospectives from several gaming publications described it as one of the best [[immersive sim]]s ever made. Arkane released an expansion named ''Mooncrash'', which adds [[procedural generation]] and gameplay elements found in [[roguelike]] games. Arkane also introduced a multiplayer update named ''Typhon Hunter'', which incorporates the Typhon shapeshifting abilities in a hide-and-seek-style game. The game's disappointing commercial performance resulted in Arkane Austin pivoting to making [[live service game|live service games]] such as ''[[Redfall]]'' (2023).

==Gameplay==
[[File:Prey 2017 gameplay screenshot.jpg|thumb|left|Players can use the Gloo Cannon to freeze Mimics, stopping them from moving and transforming into daily life objects.]]

''Prey'' is an [[immersive sim]] played from a [[first-person perspective]]. The player plays as Morgan Yu, a human who must find a way to escape a space station following its takeover by a hostile alien race named the Typhon. At the beginning of the game, the player is only equipped with a basic wrench as their weapon, though they eventually unlock a Gloo Cannon, which shoots out a foam-like substance that can freeze enemies in place.<ref name="polytips">{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/prey-guide-walkthrough/2017/5/4/15544166/items-recycler-fabricator-mimics-phantoms-skills-neuromods-weapons-status-beginners-tips-tricks/|title=Prey beginner’s guide: 18 things you need to know|first=Jeffrey|last=Parkin|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=May 4, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=August 23, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250823165436/https://www.polygon.com/prey-guide-walkthrough/2017/5/4/15544166/items-recycler-fabricator-mimics-phantoms-skills-neuromods-weapons-status-beginners-tips-tricks/|url-status=live}}</ref> The game features a number of [[firearm]]s, such as a [[Silencer (firearms)|silenced]] [[pistol]], a [[shotgun]], and a boltcaster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/prey-guide-walkthrough/2017/5/9/15595342/find-shotgun-disruptor-stun-gun-silenced-pistol-huntress-boltcaster-q-beam/|title=Prey guide: Where to find weapons|first=Jeffrey|last=Parkin|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=May 9, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=February 5, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260205010114/https://www.polygon.com/prey-guide-walkthrough/2017/5/9/15595342/find-shotgun-disruptor-stun-gun-silenced-pistol-huntress-boltcaster-q-beam/|url-status=live}}</ref> Players can also take advantage of environmental hazards, such as oil spills and explosive canisters, as well as station defenses such as [[Gun turret|turret]]s, to defeat Typhons.<ref name="GSpot tips">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/9-tips-we-wish-we-knew-before-starting-prey/2900-1225/#10|title=9 Tips We Wish We Knew Before Starting Prey|first=Miguel|last=Concepcion|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=May 10, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026}}</ref> Some movement, such as swinging a melee weapon and sprinting, consumes [[Endurance|stamina]], which gradually regenerates when the player is resting.<ref name="polytips"/> Ammo in the game is scarce, and players can make use of [[stealth game|stealth tactics]] to silently bypass enemies or chart alternate paths to avoid them entirely.<ref name="stealth">{{cite web|url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2017/05/09/a-guide-to-sneaking-through-prey-relatively-unscathed.aspx|title=A Guide To Sneaking Through Prey (Relatively) Unscathed|first=Matt|last=Bertz|work=[[Game Informer]]|date=May 9, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=May 23, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523035511/https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2017/05/09/a-guide-to-sneaking-through-prey-relatively-unscathed.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref>

There are many subspecies of Typhon in the game, each with a unique attack pattern: the Cystoids rush to players and explode; the Mimics shapeshift into common items to disguise themselves; the Poltergeists can turn themselves invisible; and the Telepaths can unleash devastating psychic energy attacks. Phantoms are human corpses taken over by the Typhon, and the power they wield is randomly generated.<ref name="GIMonster">{{cite web|url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/07/why-preys-aliens-are-different-than-anything-youve-encountered.aspx|title=Why Prey's Aliens Are Different Than Anything You've Throughout the game, the player will also encounter a singular enemy named the Nightmare, who serves as a powerful opponent that constantly hunts and stalks the player.<ref name="nightmare">{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/prey-guide-walkthrough/2017/5/10/15601656/typhon-nightmare-is-hunting-you-find-kill-hide-weapons-fight-beat/|title=Prey guide: Finding, fighting and killing the ===Expansions===
The ''Mooncrash'' expansion is a [[roguelike]] experience in which, while the layout of the station remain the same, the placement of enemies, weapons, and other items is randomized on each playthrough.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Prey: Mooncrash review: Expansion or not, this is one of 2018's best and most unique games |url=https://www.pcworld.com/article/402244/prey-mooncrash-expansion-review.html |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=PCWorld |language=en |archive-date=May 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250526152529/https://www.pcworld.com/article/402244/prey-mooncrash-expansion-review.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Marks |first=Tom |date=2018-08-11 |title=Prey: Mooncrash's Randomized Levels Were Almost Part of the Base Game |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/11/prey-mooncrashs-randomized-levels-were-almost-part-of-the-base-game |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=April 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421192458/https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/11/prey-mooncrashs-randomized-levels-were-almost-part-of-the-base-game |url-status=live }}</ref> Narratively, the player takes the role of a hacker running simulations to investigate what happened to the five survivors of the Pytheas Moonbase. In the expansion, the player must navigate each character through the station, fighting off the Typhon, collecting equipment, hacking terminals, and ultimately reaching an escape point unique to that character. The state of the station is randomized at the beginning of a run and does not reset between characters; completing a run requires escaping with all characters without dying or resetting.. Players may reset the simulation, randomizing the world elements<ref name=":2" /> and effectively starting a new run. However, the player gains points<ref name=":1" /> that they can use within the simulation to improve how any of the characters start, such as with better weapons or additional health packs, and they can permanently unlock skills for each character within future simulation runs by collecting certain objects.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-mooncrash-review | title = Prey - Mooncrash is what a triple-A roguelike should be | first = Jordan | last = Oloman | date = June 20, 2018 | access-date = June 20, 2018 | work = [[PCGamesN]] | archive-date = April 27, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200427000824/https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-mooncrash-review | url-status = live }}</ref> As players spend more time in each run, the difficulty of gameplay increases.<ref name="RPSMooncrash"/>

The ''Typhon Hunter'' expansion contains two game modes. One is designed as a single-player [[virtual reality]] experience known as Transtar VR,<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Tarason |first=Dominic |date=2018-12-11 |title=Prey: Typhon Hunter and Transtar VR out now as free Mooncrash extras |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-typhon-hunter-and-transtar-vr-out |access-date=2025-01-13 |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |language=en |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811112355/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-typhon-hunter-and-transtar-vr-out |url-status=live }}</ref> challenging the player to various [[escape room]] scenarios aboard the ''Talos I'' station.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-12-19 |title=Prey's VR Support Is A Polished, Underwhelming Escape Room Campaign |url=https://www.uploadvr.com/preys-vr-support-is-a-polished-underwhelming-escape-room-campaign/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=UploadVR |language=en |archive-date=January 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122051623/https://www.uploadvr.com/preys-vr-support-is-a-polished-underwhelming-escape-room-campaign/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The second is an asymmetrical multiplayer mode for up to six players.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prey: Mooncrash – Typhon Hunter Is Now Available |url=https://bethesda.net/en/article/3GOeNbl9yEuGgoKG82eSmQ/prey-mooncrash-typhon-hunter-coming-soon |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=bethesda.net |language=en |archive-date=January 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122051459/https://bethesda.net/en/article/3GOeNbl9yEuGgoKG82eSmQ/prey-mooncrash-typhon-hunter-coming-soon |url-status=live }}</ref> One plays as Morgan while the others are Mimic Typhons, which can disguise themselves as nearly any object within the environment.<ref name=":3" /> The player as Morgan is challenged to find and kill all the other players within a limited amount of time, while the Mimic players can rearrange items in rooms, disguise themselves, and when the Morgan player is close, jump out and attack them before seeking another hiding place.<ref name="prop hunt">{{cite web | url = https://www.vg247.com/2018/08/14/prey-typhon-hunters-multiplayer-mode-exists-garrys-mod/ | title = Prey: Typhon Hunter's multiplayer mode exists ==Plot==
===Setting===
''Prey'' takes place in an [[alternate history|alternate timeline]] where the [[Soviet Union]] encounters a species of [[eusocial]] aliens called the Typhon aboard their satellite ''Vorona 1'' in 1958. The Soviet Union works together with the United States to fight off and capture the aliens, unbeknownst to the general population. Together, they build the space station ''Kletka'',{{efn|{{langx|ru|Клетка|italic=yes}} {{lit|Cell}}}} situated in orbit around the Moon, to be used as a prison for the Typhon. After a failed assassination attempt on United States President [[John F. Kennedy]], the United States wrests full control of the ''Kletka'' satellite from the Soviet Union. Research of the Typhon continues under the name "Project Axiom". After the 1980 "Pobeg Incident", which resulted in the Typhon killing some scientists aboard the station, the American government shut down Project Axiom but left the captive Typhon alive.

In 2025, the newly founded TranStar Corporation acquires ''Kletka'' and, by 2030, refits it as ''Talos I'', a fully operational research laboratory to study the Typhon and create advances in neuroscience. This leads to the creation of Neuromods that harness the Typhon's physiology to restructure the human brain and grant the user new abilities, including superhuman ones.<ref name="ign setting slideshow">{{cite web | url = https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/05/04/these-11-images-reveal-more-about-preys-alternate-history | title = These 11 Images Reveal More About Prey's Alternate History | first = Miranda | last = Sanchez | date = May 4, 2017 | access-date = May 4, 2017 | work = [[IGN]] | archive-date = November 12, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201112025557/https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/05/04/these-11-images-reveal-more-about-preys-alternate-history | url-status = live }}</ref> TranStar grows financially successful from sales of Neuromods on Earth. At the time of the setting, about 2035, TranStar has further expanded the station to make for suitable living quarters for its staff, which spends up to two years on the station between regular shuttles to Earth.<ref name="gi story">{{cite magazine | url = https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/09/building-preys-interconnected-world.aspx | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161210002900/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/09/building-preys-interconnected-world.aspx | url-status = live | archive-date = December 10, 2016 | title = Building Prey's Interconnected World | first = Jeff | last= Cork | date = September 9, 2016 | access-date = September 9, 2016 | magazine = [[Game Informer]] }}</ref>

===Synopsis===
{{multiple image
| align       = right
| direction   = horizontal
| total_width = 300
| image1      = Benedict Wong, 2016 (cropped).jpg 
| image2      = Sumalee Montano by Gage Skidmore.jpg 
| footer      = [[Benedict Wong]] (left) and [[Sumalee Montano]] (right) played Alex Yu and the female version of Morgan Yu in ''Prey''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/prey-lets-me-be-asian|title=Prey Lets Me Be Asian|first=Steven|last=Scaife|work=[[AV Club]]|date=July 5, 2017|accessdate=February 21, 2026|archive-date=December 1, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251201034226/https://www.avclub.com/prey-lets-me-be-asian|url-status=live}}</ref>
}}

In March 2032, Morgan Yu (male voiced by [[Tim Kang]], female voiced by [[Sumalee Montano]]) is recruited by their brother Alex ([[Benedict Wong]]) to join TranStar's research team on ''Talos I''. Before leaving for the station, Morgan takes a series of tests. One of the supervising doctors is attacked by a Typhon during the testing process, and Morgan is knocked out. 

In 2035, Morgan wakes up in their apartment and finds that it is a simulated environment; they have been living on ''Talos I'' for three years. Morgan is contacted by January (voiced by Kang or Montano, depending on the player's chosen gender), an Operator [[artificial intelligence]] that claims to have been built by Morgan. January warns Morgan that the Typhon have broken containment and taken over the station, killing much of the crew. It reveals to Morgan that it and Morgan had been testing Neuromods for the past three years. While they allow for instantaneous learning of complex skills and abilities, a side effect of removing them is that the user loses all memories gained after their installation, explaining Morgan's memory loss. January claims that Morgan built it to help destroy ''Talos I'', taking the Typhon and all its research with it. Alex contacts Morgan and suggests instead building a special Nullwave device to destroy the Typhon but leave the station intact, citing that their research is too valuable to lose.

Morgan travels through the station and encounters other survivors, with players given a choice to help them or not. Alex tasks Morgan with scanning the Typhon "Coral" growing around the station and discovers that the Typhon are building a sort of neural network. Their attempts to study the neural network are interrupted when the TranStar [[Board of Directors]] learns of the containment breach and sends a cleanup crew to eliminate both the Typhon and any surviving station crew; after the cleanup crew is dealt with, Alex further analyzes the data and concludes that the Typhon are sending a signal into deep space to summon something. A gargantuan Typhon called the Apex appears and begins to devour ''Talos I''. Morgan is given the choice to activate the station's self-destruct sequence or build the Nullwave device to defeat the Typhon.

If Morgan chooses to activate the Nullwave device, all the Typhon on ''Talos I'' are destroyed and the station is left intact. If Morgan chooses to activate the self-destruct, the entire station explodes, destroying all the Typhon with it. Morgan either finds a way to escape the station or is stranded and dies in the explosion, based on earlier choices in the game. In a [[post-credits scene]], Morgan wakes up in a lab and learns that it is not the real Morgan but instead a captured Typhon implanted with Morgan's memories in an effort to teach it human emotions and empathy. The Typhon have invaded Earth; Alex and his Operator assistants judge "Morgan" based on the choices it makes throughout the game. If "Morgan" fails to show human empathy, Alex destroys it and restarts the experiment. If "Morgan" did show human empathy, Alex lets it go, whereupon it can choose to accept his offer to bring peace between the Typhon and humanity or kill him.

====''Mooncrash''====
In 2036, Peter is stationed in a remote satellite orbiting the Moon and is forced under contract by the Kasma Corporation, a rival to TranStar, to undergo numerous simulations reliving a Typhon outbreak on TranStar's Pytheas Moon Base. As he completes his assigned tasks, his handler, Basilisk, warns him that Kasma will betray him once his mission is complete and helps him prepare to escape. When Peter fulfills his contract, Kasma congratulates him but claims that due to tight budgets, they cannot retrieve him from the satellite and shut off his life support. With help from Basilisk, Peter overrides the satellite's controls and crashes it near the real Pytheas facility, where he commandeers a shuttle and returns to Earth. In a post-credits scene, it is revealed that a Mimic has stowed away on Peter's shuttle.

== Development ==
=== Origin ===
{{See also|Prey 2}}
[[File:Raphaël Colantonio, Prey Q&A, ACMI Melbourne 2017.jpg|thumb|right|180px|The game was directed by Arkane's CEO [[Raphaël Colantonio]].]]

The success of the original ''[[Prey (2006 video game)|Prey]]'' led to the announcement of ''[[Prey 2]]'' in August 2006, with continued development by [[3D Realms]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/news120706preysequel|title=Prey sequel confirmed|first=Kristen|last=Reed|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=July 12, 2006|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=August 3, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250803121018/https://www.eurogamer.net/news120706preysequel|url-status=live}}</ref> However, the project faced numerous issues, including the transfer of the [[intellectual property]] (IP) rights to [[Bethesda Softworks]] (under [[ZeniMax Media]]) and a change of developer to [[Human Head Studios]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.joystiq.com/2011/04/18/prey-2-producer-on-taking-new-direction-with-capable-id-tech|first=Jonathan D.|last=Deesing|title=Prey 2 producer on taking new direction, with 'capable' id Tech 4|work=[[Joystiq]]|publisher=Engadget|date=April 18, 2011|access-date=April 7, 2015|archive-date=October 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131013233148/http://www.joystiq.com/2011/04/18/prey-2-producer-on-taking-new-direction-with-capable-id-tech|url-status=live}}</ref>  Meanwhile, after completing work on ''[[Dishonored]]'', [[Arkane Studios]] split their team to work on two projects: ''[[Dishonored 2]]'' and a new intellectual property based on similar gameplay ideas. This new [[science fiction]]-themed game would be "in first-person, with depth and simulation and narration".<ref name="gamespot quakecon">{{cite web | url = https://www.gamespot.com/articles/prey-dev-explains-why-its-named-after-an-unrelated/1100-6442447/ | title = Prey Dev Explains Why It's Named After an Unrelated Series | first = Chris | last = Pereria | date = August 8, 2016 | access-date = August 8, 2016 | work = [[GameSpot]] | archive-date = August 4, 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220804165334/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/prey-dev-explains-why-its-named-after-an-unrelated/1100-6442447/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Development was led by Arkane Studios CEO and director [[Raphaël Colantonio]] and his team in [[Austin, Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vg247.com/2016/06/13/e3-2016-prey-re-revealed/|title=Prey coming 2017 from Dishonored dev's Austin studio|first=James|last=O'Conner|work=[[VG247]]|date=June 13, 2016|access-date=June 13, 2016|archive-date=August 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816195617/https://www.vg247.com/2016/06/13/e3-2016-prey-re-revealed/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

After Human Head's game was cancelled in 2014,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/prey-2-is-officially-cancelled|title=Prey 2 is officially cancelled|first=Matthew|last=Handrahan|work=[[Gameindustry.biz]]|date=October 31, 2014|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=January 14, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114003855/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/prey-2-is-officially-cancelled|url-status=live}}</ref> Arkane was mandated by publisher and parent company [[Bethesda Softworks]] to use the title ''Prey'' as the name of the game. At the time, the team described it as a "re-imagining of the IP", with no relation to either the original game or ''Prey 2'' outside of the player-facing aliens.<ref name="gamespot announce">{{Cite web |last=Paget |first=Mat |date=June 15, 2016 |title=New Prey Has Nothing to Do With Cancelled Prey 2, Bethesda Head Says |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-prey-has-nothing-to-do-with-cancelled-prey-2-b/1100-6440943/ |access-date=June 15, 2016 |work=[[GameSpot]] |archive-date=November 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108160114/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-prey-has-nothing-to-do-with-cancelled-prey-2-b/1100-6440943/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="gamespot prey e32016">{{cite web | url = http://www.gamespot.com/articles/prey-revealed-at-e3-2016-not-a-sequel-or-remake-up/1100-6440736/ | title = Prey Revealed at E3 2016, Not a Sequel or Remake | first = Chris | last = Pereira | date = June 12, 2016 | access-date = June 13, 2016 | work = [[GameSpot]] | archive-date = November 25, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201125004229/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/prey-revealed-at-e3-2016-not-a-sequel-or-remake-up/1100-6440736/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Colantonio said in later interviews that calling their game ''Prey'' was a decision that no one on the Arkane team was pleased with.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuhnke |first=Oisin |date=2022-09-04 |title=Prey director says he didn't want to call it that, but Bethesda insisted it should be |url=https://www.vg247.com/prey-2017-director-didnt-want-to-call-it-that |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=VG247 |language=en |archive-date=January 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250112211528/https://www.vg247.com/prey-2017-director-didnt-want-to-call-it-that |url-status=live }}</ref> They reportedly wanted their game to stand on its own as a unique IP but were overruled by corporate decisions at Bethesda, with Colantonio adding that the naming decision was "gross" and "disrespectful" to both his team and the creators of the original game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dinsdale |first=Ryan |date=2022-09-01 |title=Prey Director Says Arkane Was Forced to Use that Title: 'It's Gross... Not What I Wanted to Do' |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/prey-director-says-arkane-was-forced-to-use-that-title-its-gross-not-what-i-wanted-to-do |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=January 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250112211301/https://www.ign.com/articles/prey-director-says-arkane-was-forced-to-use-that-title-its-gross-not-what-i-wanted-to-do |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Gameplay design ===
''Prey''{{'}}s world design follows in the footsteps of games such as ''[[System Shock]]'' and Arkane's own ''[[Arx Fatalis]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usgamer.net/articles/calling-bethesdas-prey-a-metroidvania-is-a-tiny-bit-misleading/|website=USgamer|title=Calling Bethesda's Prey a Metroidvania is a Tiny Bit Misleading|first=Kat|last=Bailey|date=April 13, 2017|access-date=December 13, 2017|archive-date=April 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170414225146/http://www.usgamer.net/articles/calling-bethesdas-prey-a-metroidvania-is-a-tiny-bit-misleading/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/02/15/prey-first-hands-on-impressions-a-system-shock-of-the-best-kind|title=Prey First Hands-On Impressions: A System Shock of the Best Kind|first=Ryan|last=McCaffrey|work=[[IGN]]|date=May 3, 2017|accessdate=March 24, 2026}}</ref> Colantonio described ''Prey'' as an "open structure" game in which the entire game is a long, self-contained mission where players can return to the same area repeatedly.<ref name="skyscraper">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/prey-is-metroidvania-in-a-skyscraper-floating-in-space/|website=GamesRadar+|title=Prey is Metroidvania in a "skyscraper floating in space"|first=Leon|last=Hurley|date=August 5, 2016|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=December 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251207015700/https://www.gamesradar.com/prey-is-metroidvania-in-a-skyscraper-floating-in-space/|url-status=live}}</ref> The team followed the "mega-dungeon" concept of ''Arx Fatalis'' but set it in a space station filled with hostile aliens. Players were required to consider the "full ecology" of the game world to overcome obstacles that gate their progress,<ref name="gamespot quakecon"/><ref name="gamasutra dungeon"/> ranging from overpowered enemy encounters to the station's collapsing infrastructure.<ref name="skyscraper"/> They did not want the player to solve singular-solution puzzles, such as simply finding a key for a locked door, but instead to use the game's full suite of tools to overcome an interconnected environment that was challenging for exploration. The team described ''Talos I'' as a "living, dynamic world" that provided many viable solutions to the same problem.<ref name="gamasutra dungeon"/> [[Metroidvania]] games were also a key influence on gameplay design.<ref name="noclip"/> Designer Ricardo Bare described the space station as a "skyscraper floating in space".<ref name="skyscraper"/> As a corporate experimental facility, it was designed to be functional and believable, with all the rooms and utilities required by a fully staffed location.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/09/building-preys-interconnected-world.aspx|title=Building Prey’s Interconnected World|first=Jeff|last=Cork|work=[[Game Informer]]|date=December 9, 2016|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251213141401/https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/09/building-preys-interconnected-world.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> Climbable [[ladder]]s were one of the transversal mechanics that the team actively avoided in ''Prey''.<ref name="ladder"/> Bare added that designing freeform gameplay was "tricky" as players may appear in any part of the station regardless of progress. Since the game did not limit players' action, fixing bugs was stated to be the team's biggest technical challenge.<ref name="pcgamesn bare">{{Cite web | url = https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-builds-characters-turret-lord | title = Prey's origins in Arx Fatalis and the legend of the Turret Lord with lead designer Ricardo Bare | first = Ben | last = Barrett | date = March 17, 2017 | access-date = March 17, 2017 | work = [[PCGamesN]] | archive-date = August 16, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170816232840/https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-builds-characters-turret-lord | url-status = live }}</ref> 

''Prey'' incorporates numerous gameplay concepts from ''Dishonored'', where players are encouraged to find creative solutions to overcome obstacles.<ref name="gi dishonored">{{cite magazine | url = https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/28/arkane-knowledge-five-reasons-dishonored-fans-will-love-prey.aspx | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161229050921/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/28/arkane-knowledge-five-reasons-dishonored-fans-will-love-prey.aspx | url-status = live | archive-date = December 29, 2016 | title = Arkane Knowledge: Five Reasons Dishonored Fans Will Love Prey | first = Ben | last= Reeves | date = December 28, 2016 | access-date = December 29, 2016 | magazine = [[Game Informer]] }}</ref> Borrowed elements from ''Dishonored'' include giving the player enough agency to determine how they want to proceed, developing a game world based on pre-established lore that can be learned by examining notes and computer terminals throughout the station, and a simple user interface.<ref name="gi dishonored"/> However, Colantonio said that ''Prey'' was less focused on stealth than ''Dishonored'' and provided a more [[role-playing video game]]-style improvement system through in-game chipsets that allow the player to customize their abilities.<ref name="gi dishonored"/> The developers also took inspiration from ''[[FTL: Faster Than Light]]'', considering the complexities of the various gameplay systems and the speed at which a situation can go wrong if the player did not sufficiently plan; Bare said they wanted to include that "chaos of systems", in which failing station systems and the decaying infrastructure of ''Talos I'' created [[environmental hazard]]s that can be both an aid to the players in defeating the Typhon or a cause of unforeseen consequences if the player is not careful.<ref name="FTL">{{Cite web | url = https://www.polygon.com/2017/4/13/15290658/prey-video-preview | title = Watch an hour of new Prey footage | first = Arthur | last = Gies | date = April 13, 2017 | access-date = May 10, 2017 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] | archive-date = April 30, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170430145242/http://www.polygon.com/2017/4/13/15290658/prey-video-preview | url-status = live }}</ref> Arkane had considered including [[procedural generation]] within the main campaign so that different areas may have different hazards when encountered. However, as they believed it would frustrate players and cause them to skip content, they dropped this approach for ''Prey'' and worked it into ''Mooncrash'' instead.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/11/prey-mooncrashs-randomized-levels-were-almost-part-of-the-base-game | title = Prey: Mooncrash's Randomized Levels Were Almost Part Of The Base Game | first = Tom | last = Marks | date = August 11, 2018 | access-date = August 11, 2018 | work = [[IGN]] | archive-date = August 11, 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180811181819/http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/11/prey-mooncrashs-randomized-levels-were-almost-part-of-the-base-game | url-status = live }}</ref>

[[Emergent gameplay]] was a goal of Arkane: while they had given the players abilities to take on ''Prey'' in a full action mode or full stealth mode, they wanted players to find a way to complete the game in their own manner,<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> improvising using the game's various systems.<ref name="ladder">{{cite web|url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/14/f-ladders-and-19-other-design-mantras-for-arkanes-prey.aspx|title='F*** Ladders', And 19 Other Design Mantras For Arkane's Prey|first=Ben|last=Hansen|work=[[Game Informer]]|date=December 14, 2016|accessdate=February 19, 2026}}</ref> They avoided including enemies or obstacles that would be impossible to surpass because a player did not specialize in the right skills and provided a means to bypass such areas.<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> One of the Typhon aliens, the Mimic, was inspired by [[Mimic (Dungeons & Dragons)|the creature of the same name]] from ''[[Dungeons & Dragons]]'' and was programmed to take the form of any object smaller than itself in the room without the use of scripted events, instead allowing the alien's [[Artificial intelligence (video games)|artificial intelligence]] to decide what to replicate.<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> The Psychoscope, which allows players to scan an alien to learn and use its powers, also created new but unexpected gameplay options, such as taking the form of a small object to sneak into small places or taking the form of a non-flammable object to roll through fire-laden areas.<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> Inspired by ''Dishonored'', ''Prey'' had in-game consequences of both an emotional and a mechanical nature for certain player actions. How the player interacts with its cast of [[non-playable character]]s may alter its ending,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.redbull.com/gb-en/prey-2017-arkane-studios-interview|title=Prey: All your favourite sci-fi movies in one game|first=Jon|last=Partridge|work=[[Red Bull]]|date=May 5, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026}}</ref> and using too many Typhon upgrades may result in gameplay alterations.<ref name="station defense">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/arkane-studios-the-story-so-far-history|title=Arkane Studios: The Story So Far|first=Matt|last=Purslow|work=[[IGN]]|date=September 25, 2021|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=August 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814034820/https://www.ign.com/articles/arkane-studios-the-story-so-far-history|url-status=live}}</ref>

Arkane recognized that as a research station, ''Talos I''<nowiki/>'s security forces would likely only have common weapons, such as pistols and shotguns, and advanced weapons were designed to look like flawed prototypes only in their testing phases.<ref name="gamasutra dungeon"/> Their design was inspired by Stanley Greenberg's ''Time Machine'', a book featuring photographs of stylized experimental prototypes, and drew from a [[CERN]] database detailing their experiments from the 1960s and 70s.<ref name="TG art"/> While direct confrontations with enemies are an option, many of the tools in ''Prey'' allow players to take advantage of enemies, disabling them before striking.<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> One of the weapons, the Gloo Cannon, allowed players to freeze enemies in place and create makeshift platforms for exploration. As the moon station setting provided a clear boundary, the team felt that players should be allowed to move through this space freely and fluidly. This created pressure for the art team, who had to ensure that every corner of the game was well-designed. An early mechanic allowed players to directly fly through the space station; it was scrapped. Due to technical constraints of the game's console versions, gloo must always attach to an object in the game's world.<ref name="gloo">{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-making-of-preys-gloo-cannon/|title=The making of Prey's Gloo Cannon|first=Joe|last=Donnelly|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=July 4, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026}}</ref>

=== Story and narrative ===
[[File:JFK Motorcade GettyImages-517330536.jpg|thumb|left|One of the points of divergence in ''Prey''{{'}}s [[Parallel universe (fiction)|parallel universe]] is the failed [[assassination of John F. Kennedy]].]]
According to design documents from the project's early history, the game was developed at Arkane under the name "Project Danielle",<ref name="Kotaku">{{cite web | url = http://kotaku.com/old-leaked-design-documents-show-what-prey-couldve-been-1795295577 | title = Old Leaked Design Documents Show What Prey Could've Been | first = Jason | last = Schreier | author-link = Jason Schreier | date = May 17, 2017 | access-date = May 19, 2017 | work = [[Kotaku]] | archive-date = May 17, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170517200854/http://kotaku.com/old-leaked-design-documents-show-what-prey-couldve-been-1795295577 | url-status = live }}</ref> a title that paid homage to [[SHODAN]] from ''[[System Shock]]''.<ref name="noclip">{{cite AV media |date=September 15, 2021 |title=The Making of Prey - Documentary |type=Motion picture |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kXLxaKrcFZ0 |access-date=January 23, 2024 |time=4:55 |via=YouTube |publisher=[[Noclip]] |archive-date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240123175454/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kXLxaKrcFZ0 |url-status=live }}</ref> Three different concepts were presented, all based on the nature of ''System Shock'' and involving the player-character, Danielle Sho, discovering the false reality in their apparent world and interacting with an [[artificial intelligence]] with significant influence on events; settings included a futuristic lab set on Earth, a secret lab on a remote island, and a retro-futuristic setting.<ref name="Kotaku" /> The opening sequence, which serves as a fake tutorial and sees Morgan discovering their life as a simulation, was created by the team to set the tone for the game and establish a feeling of distrust within players.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GLExoItBLVc|title=How Prey's Mind-Bending Opening Level Was Designed|work=[[Noclip]]|date=August 5, 2020|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=February 15, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215133103/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GLExoItBLVc|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/get-some-design-advice-from-i-prey-i-lead-designer-ricardo-bare|title=Get some design advice from Prey lead designer Ricardo Bare|first=Bryant|last=Francis|work=[[Game Developer (magazine)|Game Developer]]|date=May 12, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=May 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220516162940/https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/get-some-design-advice-from-i-prey-i-lead-designer-ricardo-bare|url-status=live}}</ref> Arkane restricted the number of horror elements they included, since they could not predict the path of the player or where the player's attention would be.<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> Instead, Colantonio described the game as a "psychological thriller".<ref name="gspot influence"/>

The narrative concept for ''Prey'' came to Colantonio on a flight while traveling.<ref name="bethblog story">{{cite web | url = https://bethesda.net/en/article/3QUOVPanDO4gOSKiQCgW8K/crafting-the-story-of-prey | title = Crafting the Story of Prey | first = Gary | last = Steinman | date = April 25, 2017 | access-date = May 9, 2017 | website = [[Bethesda Softworks]] | archive-date = August 16, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170816193034/https://bethesda.net/en/article/3QUOVPanDO4gOSKiQCgW8K/crafting-the-story-of-prey | url-status = live }}</ref><ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> Colantonio said that it took about a year from this initial concept to come up with an alternate timeline that helped support this detailing.<ref name="bethblog story"/> They considered how the future would have been different if [[John F. Kennedy]] survived the [[Assassination of John F. Kennedy|assassination attempt]], allowing them to flesh out the narrative and design of the space station.<ref name="pcgamesn bare"/> As ''Talos I'' is a relatively small space, Arkane was able to detail the station in-depth to make the world more cohesive, such as naming and fleshing out background stories for each [[non-player character]] (NPC), including those already dead when the story begins.<ref name="daily dot"/> As with other [[immersive sim]]s, the game placed a large emphasis on [[environmental storytelling]], making extensive use of books, notes, and audio logs to provide additional information regarding the setting and the lore. Bare added that these storytelling efforts were essential for players to understand the location better, though the team accepted that not all players will discover them due to their optional nature. Bare added that by giving the player a choice to examine or completely ignore them, ''Talos I'' became a setting that felt more "real". As the game was largely nonlinear, the discovery of this optional content also became individualized, creating a story that felt personal.<ref name="nonlinear">{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2017-06-05-prey-arkane-alternate-history-space-race.html|title=How the studio behind 'Prey' reimagined space history|first=Nick|last=Summers|work=[[Engadget]]|date=June 5, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=August 16, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250816155404/https://www.engadget.com/2017-06-05-prey-arkane-alternate-history-space-race.html|url-status=live}}</ref> To keep the game immersive, the game rarely took players out of gameplay and had a minimal amount of non-interactive [[cutscene]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamereactor.eu/arkanes-raphael-colantonio-discusses-storytelling-methods/|title=Arkane's Raphael Colantonio discusses storytelling methods|first=Sam|last=Bishop|work=Gamereactor|date=December 16, 2016|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=March 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326022627/https://www.gamereactor.eu/arkanes-raphael-colantonio-discusses-storytelling-methods/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Austin Grossman]], also of Arkane, helped establish early plot details.<ref name="bethblog story"/> Bare reached out to [[Chris Avellone]] in around 2013 for help with the story,<ref name="bethblog story"/> and Avellone worked with Arkane on the story from June to about November 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.polygon.com/e3/2016/6/13/11919114/chris-avellone-prey-2-bethesda-arkane-studios | title = Ex-Obsidian chief creative officer Chris Avellone is working on the new Prey | first = Michael | last = McWhertor | date = June 13, 2016 | access-date = May 9, 2017 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] | archive-date = April 13, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200413020103/https://www.polygon.com/e3/2016/6/13/11919114/chris-avellone-prey-2-bethesda-arkane-studios | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-chris-avellone | title = Chris Avellone says he's "been wrapped up with Prey for a while now" | first = Kirk | last = McKeand | date = November 22, 2016 | access-date = May 9, 2017 | work = [[PCGamesN]] | archive-date = September 24, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200924045251/https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-chris-avellone | url-status = live }}</ref> Avellone also contributed to designing several NPCs and the various missions that involved them. He felt these characters and their missions created dilemmas for the player, helping the player define their version of Morgan as well as expanding on the game universe.<ref name="bethblog story"/> Among other works, ''Prey'' was influenced by the films ''[[Moon (2009 film)|Moon]]'', ''[[Starship Troopers (film)|Starship Troopers]]'', and ''[[The Matrix (1999 film)|The Matrix]]''. As part of promotional efforts, Bethesda partnered with the [[Alamo Drafthouse]] to show these three films in April 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://venturebeat.com/2017/03/24/bethesda-partners-with-alamo-drafthouse-for-films-that-inspired-prey/ | title = Bethesda partners with Alamo Drafthouse to show 'The Matrix' and other films that inspired Prey | first = Jeff | last = Grubb | date = March 24, 2017 | access-date = March 24, 2017 | work = [[Venture Beat]] | archive-date = August 6, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210806164918/https://venturebeat.com/2017/03/24/bethesda-partners-with-alamo-drafthouse-for-films-that-inspired-prey/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Avellone also cited ''[[Aliens (film)|Aliens]]'' as part of his inspiration, describing it as an action-suspense film that has moments of comedy, even amid heavy action sequences, something he reused in  ''Prey''.<ref name="bethblog story"/> ''[[Sunshine (2007 film)|Sunshine]]'', ''[[Total Recall (2012 film)|Total Recall]]'', and [[Lovecraftian]] fiction also influenced the game.<ref name="gspot influence">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/prey-boss-talks-influences-aliens-pc-version-and-m/1100-6449757/|title=Prey Boss Talks Influences, Aliens, PC Version, And Mor|first=Eddie|last=Makuch|work=[[GameSpot]]|date=May 5, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026}}</ref>

===Art design===
[[File:Chicago world's fair, a century of progress, expo poster, 1933, 2.jpg|thumb|180px|The art direction of the game was inspired by [[Art Deco]].]]
The styles used in the various parts of the station were directly attributed to the [[alternate history]] fiction itself, with the team considering what architecture would have influenced those most responsible for operating ''Talos I'' at the time. This ranged from considering the visual motifs during the Kennedy era to envisioning how those funding contemporary [[Commercial use of space|commercial space efforts]], like [[Elon Musk]] or Google, would style a space station.<ref name="gamasutra dungeon"/> Because of the numerous agencies that operated and expanded ''Talos I'' over the decades, the station includes a large mix of architectural designs, ranging from [[retrofuturism]] that was popular in 1960s America to [[Brutalist architecture|brutalist]] styles that were common in the Soviet Bloc in the mid-20th century to opulent [[Art Deco]] put in place by the wealthy TranStar executives.<ref name="gamasutra dungeon">{{cite web | url = https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/designing-i-prey-i-s-sci-fi-space-station-to-be-like-a-mega-dungeon- | title = Designing Prey's sci-fi space station to be like a 'mega-dungeon' | first = Roy | last = Graham | date = May 4, 2017 | access-date = May 4, 2017 | work = [[Gamasutra]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170505042453/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/297288/Designing_Preys_scifi_space_station_to_be_like_a_megadungeon.php | archive-date = May 5, 2017 | url-status = live}}</ref><ref name="vg247 alttime">{{cite web | url = https://www.vg247.com/2016/09/09/preys-alternate-timeline-depicts-a-future-where-jfk-lived-to-see-the-space-program-flourish/ | title = Prey's alternate timeline depicts a future where JFK lived to see the space program flourish | first = Stephany | last = Nunneley | date = September 9, 2016 | access-date = September 9, 2016 | work = [[VG247]] | archive-date = March 29, 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190329005312/https://www.vg247.com/2016/09/09/preys-alternate-timeline-depicts-a-future-where-jfk-lived-to-see-the-space-program-flourish/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Artist Sébastien Mitton described the game's art style as "Neo Deco", which merged futuristic elements into aesthetics of the mid-20th century. The team was also influenced by the works of architect [[Hugh Ferriss]], painter [[John Berkey]], the design of [[NASA]]'s early spacecraft, the Viceroy hotel in New York, and unrealized projects such as [[South Ferry Plaza]]. The entrance Lobby of ''Talos I'' was the first location created, and its furnishing and interior design were influenced by the works of [[Frank Lloyd Wright]] and [[Wilhelm Wagenfeld]],<ref name="TG art">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2017/jul/26/building-prey-game-developer-arkane-artists-shape-video-game-worlds|title=Building Prey: how artists shape video game worlds|first=Keith|last=Stuart|work=[[The Guardian (website)|The Guardian]]|date=July 26, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026}}</ref> while the technology in the game was inspired by that created by [[International Business Machines|IBM]] and consumer electronic designer [[Jacob Jensen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/21/a-deeper-look-at-preys-striking-neo-deco-design.aspx|title=A Deeper Look At Prey’s Striking ‘Neo Deco’ Design|first=Jeff|last=Cork|work=[[Game Informer]]|date=December 21, 2016|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=February 10, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260210141836/https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2016/12/21/a-deeper-look-at-preys-striking-neo-deco-design.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> The team also created a lot of TranStar posters and decorations and placed them all over ''Talos I'', as they were inspired by Ansgar Oswald's book "Offices Construction and Design Manual" which documented how corporate identity "permeates the workplace".<ref name="TG art"/>

Arkane's [[Harvey Smith (game designer)|Harvey Smith]] is credited with establishing the Typhon and the reason for their existence in the story.<ref name="bethblog story"/>  Arkane wanted a more unique design for the aliens and opted to use designs inspired by [[paranormal]] elements rather than stereotypical insect- or lizard-like species.<ref name="daily dot">{{cite web | url = https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/prey-arkane-studios-interview/ | title = Unraveling the story of Arkane Studios' mysterious shooter, Prey | first = AJ | last = Moser | date = May 4, 2017 | access-date = May 5, 2017 | work = [[Daily Dot]] | archive-date = April 15, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210415232824/https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/prey-arkane-studios-interview/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Colantonio wanted the monsters in the game to be black in color, and the team came up with designs that were "visually undefined, mysterious, blurry" whose complexities were entirely reflected through their [[silhouette]]s. They were inspired by [[time-lapse photography]] of people in motion, particularly the ''Metamorphosis'' series by Frederic Fontenoy. Additional [[particle effect]]s and blurry animated shaders were added to these monsters to make them look more enigmatic. The animation team was inspired by the movement of real-life animals, such as [[praying mantis|praying mantises]], [[octopus]]es, and [[squid]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-typhon-design|title=State of the Art: The monsters of Prey|first=Philipa|last=Warr|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=June 27, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=January 22, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122213441/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-typhon-design|url-status=live}}</ref> The Typhons in the game had their own ecology. For instance, Mimics served as scouts for the Typhon and can combine together to form another enemy variant named Weaver.<ref name="gspot influence"/> The Nightmare, a powerful Typhon that shows up regularly to hunt the player, was inspired by the [[Xenomorph|Alien]] from ''[[Alien: Isolation]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/prey-is-more-freaky-sci-fi-less-horror/|title=‘Prey’ Is More Freaky Sci-fi, Less Horror|first=Danielle|last=Riendeau|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|date=February 16, 2017|accessdate=February 24, 2026}}</ref>

The original score was composed and produced by [[Mick Gordon (composer)|Mick Gordon]], who had previously composed the soundtrack for ''[[Doom (2016 video game)|Doom]]'' (2016). Additional music was composed by Ben Crossbones, Matt Piersall, and Colantonio, with each one providing a single track. The soundtrack was released for live-streaming music services a week before the game's release.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.gamespot.com/articles/listen-to-preys-eerie-and-atmospheric-soundtrack-r/1100-6449748/ | title = Listen To Prey's Eerie And Atmospheric Soundtrack Right Now | first = Eddie | last = Makuch | date = May 2, 2017 | access-date = May 2, 2017 | work = [[GameSpot]] | archive-date = December 13, 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181213181542/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/listen-to-preys-eerie-and-atmospheric-soundtrack-r/1100-6449748/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

==Release and marketing==
Bethesda announced ''Prey'' during its press conference at [[E3 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-arkane-e3|title=Arkane Announce Prey: Immersive Horror Sim|first=Adam|last=Smith|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=June 13, 2016|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=November 2, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241102184026/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-arkane-e3|url-status=live}}</ref> The game was released on May 5, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://venturebeat.com/2017/01/25/prey-will-bring-you-more-aliens-to-slaughter-on-may-5/ | title = Prey will bring you more aliens to slaughter on May 5 | first = Dean | last = Takahashi | date = January 25, 2017 | access-date = January 25, 2017 | work = [[VentureBeat]] | archive-date = January 25, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170125155146/http://venturebeat.com/2017/01/25/prey-will-bring-you-more-aliens-to-slaughter-on-may-5/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> Players who pre-ordered the game received the "Cosmonaut Shotgun Pack", which offered several in-game weapons and consumables for players to use.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/01/25/prey-release-date-announced-2|title=Prey Release Date Announced|first=Andrew|last=Goldfarb|work=[[IGN]]|date=May 3, 2017|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=December 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241223033045/https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/01/25/prey-release-date-announced-2|url-status=live}}</ref> Just prior to release, No Matter Studios, the developers of ''Prey for the Gods'', announced that they had to change the name of their game to ''[[Praey for the Gods]]'' due to trademark objections from ZeniMax Media. ZeniMax reported that they had to defend the ''Prey'' trademark to avoid losing it by taking objection to No Matter's trademark filing.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.polygon.com/2017/5/3/15534924/prey-for-the-gods-praey-for-the-gods-trademark-name-change | title = Prey for the Gods changes name to avoid fight with Bethesda's Prey | first = Allegra | last = Frank | date = May 3, 2017 | access-date = May 8, 2017 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] | archive-date = October 31, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201031234815/https://www.polygon.com/2017/5/3/15534924/prey-for-the-gods-praey-for-the-gods-trademark-name-change | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.polygon.com/2017/5/8/15572464/zenimax-bethesda-prey-for-the-dead-trademark | title = ZeniMax has to protect Prey, even if it looks like a bully while doing so | first = John | last = Warren | date = May 8, 2017 | access-date = May 8, 2017 | work = [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] | archive-date = June 3, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200603092452/https://www.polygon.com/2017/5/8/15572464/zenimax-bethesda-prey-for-the-dead-trademark | url-status = live }}</ref> Arkane and Bethesda provided a [[game demo]] for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One consoles about a week before the launch, covering about the first hour of gameplay. The studio did not opt to provide a demo for Windows systems, citing that they had to choose between either the consoles or personal computers for demo release. Colantonio said that with the release through [[Steam (service)|Steam]], interested players can try the game for up to two hours under Steam's return policy, effectively treating this as the equivalent of a demo.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.ausgamers.com/news/read/3574291/preys-raph-colantonio-says-steams-2-hour-refund-policy-stands-in-place-of-demo | title = Prey's Raph Colantonio Says Steam's 2 Hour Refund Policy Stands in Place of Demo | author = Joaby | date = May 3, 2017 | access-date = May 3, 2017 | work = [[AusGamers]] | archive-date = April 1, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200401180512/https://www.ausgamers.com/news/read/3574291/preys-raph-colantonio-says-steams-2-hour-refund-policy-stands-in-place-of-demo | url-status = live }}</ref> The Steam version eventually received a demo in August 2017, which included roughly the first hour of gameplay.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chalk |first1=Andy |title=A free Prey demo is now available on Steam |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/a-free-trial-version-of-prey-is-now-available-on-steam/ |website=[[PC Gamer]] |publisher=[[Future plc]] |access-date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818121501/https://www.pcgamer.com/a-free-trial-version-of-prey-is-now-available-on-steam/ |archive-date=August 18, 2017 |date=August 16, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

=== Expansions ===
During [[E3 2018]], Bethesda announced and released a free update that added two new game modes to ''Prey'', including a [[New Game Plus]] mode and a Survival mode that adds modifiers, such as weapon durability, that make it more difficult. The first paid expansion, ''Mooncrash'', was also released on the same day.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://kotaku.com/preys-dlc-is-called-mooncrash-infinitely-replayable-1826717511 | title = Prey's DLC Is Called Mooncrash, 'Infinitely Replayable' | first = Riley | last = McCloud | date = June 10, 2018 | access-date = June 10, 2018 | work = [[Kotaku]] | archive-date = November 30, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201130114706/https://kotaku.com/preys-dlc-is-called-mooncrash-infinitely-replayable-1826717511 | url-status = live }}</ref> [[Roguelike]] elements were added to the game, as the team wanted to evolve the [[immersive sim]] formula while preserving the core gameplay of ''Prey''. Realizing that most players will not fully explore the entire space station due to the main game's linear plot structure, ''Mooncrash'' was designed to be a shorter game meant to be replayed many times. It adopted a more open-ended narrative, and each character starts and ends at a different location of the moon station, so players will explore the same station using various routes.<ref name="RPSMooncrash">{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/why-arkane-went-roguelike-with-preys-mooncrash-dlc|title=Why Arkane went roguelike with Prey's Mooncrash DLC|first=Tom|last=Francis|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=March 26, 2019|accessdate=February 18, 2026|archive-date=February 11, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211150640/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/why-arkane-went-roguelike-with-preys-mooncrash-dlc|url-status=live}}</ref> The expansion was further updated in September 2018 with a free patch that provided in-game customization skins that celebrated the team's favorite roguelike games, which included ''[[Spelunky]]'', ''[[Rogue Legacy]]'', ''[[Risk of Rain]]'', ''[[Don't Starve]]'', ''[[Darkest Dungeon]]'', and ''[[Dead Cells]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.destructoid.com/prey-mooncrash-update-adds-roguelike-skin-homages-521363.phtml | title = Prey: Mooncrash update adds roguelike skin homages | first = Chris | last = Carter | date = September 5, 2018 | access-date = September 5, 2018 | work = [[Destructoid]] | archive-date = November 9, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201109032923/https://www.destructoid.com/prey-mooncrash-update-adds-roguelike-skin-homages-521363.phtml | url-status = dead }}</ref>

The ''Typhon Hunt'' mode was inspired by the "Prop Hunt" mode that came about from ''[[Garry's Mod]]''; as Arkane started to show initial details of the main game, including the Mimic enemies, players responded that they were reminded of "Prop Hunt". Bare had not been aware of what that was, but after researching it, felt it was ideal for a multiplayer extension of ''Prey''.<ref name="prop hunt"/>  The ''Typhon Hunt'' mode was released on December 11, 2018, along with a [[virtual reality]]-based [[escape the room|escape-the-room]] set of puzzles set before the events of ''Prey''. Both modes were released as free additions to ''Mooncrash''.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2018/12/06/prey-multiplayer-and-vr-free-next-week/ | title = Prey: Mooncrash adds free paranoid multiplayer and VR escape rooms next week | first = Dominic | last = Tarason | date = December 6, 2018 | access-date = December 6, 2018 | work = [[Rock Paper Shotgun]] | archive-date = October 25, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201025052737/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2018/12/06/prey-multiplayer-and-vr-free-next-week/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Both ''Mooncrash'' and ''Typhon Hunt'' were modes prototyped within an internal [[game jam]] following the release of ''Prey'', looking to see how they could easily extend the game.<ref name="prop hunt"/>

| TG = 3/5<ref name="TGRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2017/may/08/prey-review-sci-fi-shooter-bioshock-dead-space-dishonored-bethesda|title=Prey review: sci-fi shooter mashup is less than sum of its parts|first=Hirun|last=Cryer|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=May 8, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026}}</ref>
}}

''Prey'' received "generally favorable" reviews from critics, according to [[review aggregator]] [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCPC"/><ref name="MCPS4"/><ref name="MCXONE"/> Several critics recognized ''Prey'' as one of the year's best games.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--staff writer--> |date=December 29, 2017 |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-12-29-eurogamers-top-50-games-of-2017-20-11 |title=Eurogamer's Top 50 Games of 2017: 20-11 |website=[[Eurogamer]] |access-date=December 31, 2017 |archive-date=January 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20180109001125/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-12-29-eurogamers-top-50-games-of-2017-20-11 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--staff |archive-url=https://archive.today/20180326130308/https://www.gamesradar.com/best-games-2017/2/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--staff writer--> |date=December 18, 2017
