|archive-date=March 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331191219/https://www.polygon.com/2017-best-games/2017/12/18/16781674/best-video-games-2017-top-50-mario-pubg-zelda |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--staff writer--> |date=December 30, 2017 |url=http://www.egmnow.com/articles/features/egms-best-of-2017-part-four-10-6/ |title=EGM's Best of 2017: Part Four: #10 ~ #6 |publisher=EGMNow |access-date=January 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20180117072822/http://www.egmnow.com/articles/features/egms-best-of-2017-part-four-10-6/ |archive-date=January 17, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was nominated for "Best Storytelling" at the [[Golden Joystick Awards]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gaming/news/public-voting-2017-golden-joystick-awards-nominees/|title=Public voting and the nominations for the 2017 Golden Joystick Awards are now up|first=Hannah|last=Dawn|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=October 27, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=January 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103072635/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/gaming/news/public-voting-2017-golden-joystick-awards-nominees/|url-status=live}}</ref> "Best Action Game" at [[The Game Awards 2017|The Game Awards]],<ref name="winners">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/all-the-2017-game-awards-winners-revealed/1100-6455467/ |title=All The 2017 Game Awards Winners Revealed |last=Makuch |first=Eddie |date=December 7, 2017 |website=GameSpot |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171208045006/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/all-the-2017-game-awards-winners-revealed/1100-6455467/ |archive-date=December 8, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> and "Excellence in Narrative" at the [[SXSW Gaming Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |author=IGN Studios |date=March 17, 2018 |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/03/18/sxsw-gaming-awards-2018-winners-revealed |title=2018 SXSW Gaming Awards Winners Revealed |website=IGN |access-date=March 18, 2018 |archive-date=March 18, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318113052/http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/03/18/sxsw-gaming-awards-2018-winners-revealed |url-status=live }}</ref>

Dan Stepleton from ''[[IGN]]'' described the setting as "sophisticated", adding that the game's open structure provided many alternative pathways for players to reach their objective. He remarked that despite needing to revisit locations to complete quests, it did not become repetitive, as new skills are unlocked to aid exploration.<ref name="IGNRev"/> Phil Savage from ''[[PC Gamer]]'' wrote that the location felt "natural", praising its realistic environmental design and room layout that is rooted in utility.<ref name="PCGRev"/> Critics generally enjoyed Arkane's level design, praising their efforts in designing a complex layout for the space station and ensuring that each location has multiple points of access, some of which can be reached through unconventional ways.<ref name="IGNRev"/><ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/5/8/15581242/prey-review-xbox-one-ps4-pc-bethesda-arkane|title=Prey is a complex, tense, and scattered piece of survival horror|first=Adi|last=Robertson|work=[[The Verge]]|date=May 8, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=May 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170508222441/https://www.theverge.com/2017/5/8/15581242/prey-review-xbox-one-ps4-pc-bethesda-arkane|url-status=live}}</ref> Tina Amini from ''[[Mashable]]'' described the station as a "maze" and liked how players need to take time to master its layout.<ref name="mashable">{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/article/prey-review|title=Review: ‘Prey’ is a tough game that asks tough questions|first=Tina|last=Amini|work=[[The Verge]]|date=May 17, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=December 2, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202141255/https://mashable.com/article/prey-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Javy Gwaltney from ''[[Game Informer]]'' praised ''Prey'' for its "sense of wonder", and Tamoor Hussain from ''[[GameSpot]]'' described the game as visually striking, though they both felt that the station was not visually diverse enough.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/>  Critics applauded its environmental storytelling and side quests, which follow the crews of ''Talos I'' and their struggles.<ref name="GRadarRev"/><ref name="RPSRev"/><ref name="IGNRev"/><ref name="PolyRev"/>

''[[GamesRadar]]''{{'}} Zoe Delahunty-Light liked the incorporation of alien powers, though she felt that the human skills were underdeveloped comparatively.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Gwaltney praised the game's enemy variety and described them as "unnerving". He praised its immersive sim elements, writing that the interlocking systems, despite being complicated, created memorable yet emergent gameplay.<ref name="GIRev"/> John Walker from ''[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]'' praised how the game gave players freedom to use its systems. Observing the game's restraint in explaining its gameplay, he wrote that the game let players "improvise, explore, make big decisions without needing to tell you they’re big".<ref name="RPSRev">{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-review|title=Wot I Think: Prey|first=John|last=Walker|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=May 9, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=January 14, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114030434/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/prey-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'', Arthur Gies commented that the game rewarded players for experimentation. Despite noting the game's high difficulty, he felt that it contributed to its "ominous, foreboding mood".<ref name="PolyRev"/> Several reviewers criticized the early part of the game for being sluggish to play, as players had not yet unlocked the tools and upgrades necessary to make combat interesting.<ref name="RPSRev"/><ref name="GIRev"/><ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="PCGRev"/> Stapleton remarked that combat was one of the game's weaknesses, criticizing its uninteresting weapons, and bare-bones stealth mechanics, and remarking that certain alien powers were too overpowered and enemies had too much [[health (gaming)|health]].<ref name="IGNRev"/>  Several critics disliked fighting Mimics because they were too agile, with Hussain criticizing the gunplay for not being responsive.<ref name="GSpotRev"/><ref name="RPSRev"/> Savage wrote that its shortcomings were a result of the game catering to a vast spectrum of playstyles, making none of its mechanics as refined as other games like ''[[BioShock]]'' or Arkane's own ''Dishonored''.<ref name="PCGRev"/>

The narrative of the game received a mixed reception. Gies enjoyed how the game built up a sense of distrust and compared ''Prey'' to ''[[Solaris (1972 film)|Solaris]]'', a psychological thriller.<ref name="PolyRev"/> Delahunty-Light liked that all characters, even the deceased, are named, and that their stories are reflected through the audio logs and emails found in the game.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Gwaltney praised the game's exploration of Yu's morality and how these moral choices affect the narrative and described Morgan's interactions with other characters as one of the game's highlights.<ref name="GIRev"/> The main quest, however, was criticized for being light in story.<ref name="GRadarRev"/> Stepleton and Hussain praised the game's tutorial but felt that it foreshadowed a much more interesting narrative than what the actual story ended up being.<ref name="IGNRev"/> Tamoor further criticized the quests for being uninspiring and felt that both the story and its characters were not memorable.<ref name="GSpotRev"/> Several reviewers also criticized its pacing for being uneven and commented that the game frequently forced players to backtrack to extend its story and runtime.<ref name="mashable"/><ref name="TGRev"/> The game was praised by several critics and journalists for having an Asian protagonist.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Takahashi|first=Dean|date=May 5, 2017|title=Bethesda's Prey gives us a rare Asian main character in a blockbuster game|url=https://venturebeat.com/2017/05/05/bethesdas-prey-gives-us-a-rare-asian-main-character-in-a-blockbuster-game/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505234807/https://venturebeat.com/2017/05/05/bethesdas-prey-gives-us-a-rare-asian-main-character-in-a-blockbuster-game/|archive-date=May 5, 2017|access-date=October 23, 2020|website=VentureBeat|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Valdes|first=Giancarlo|date=March 13, 2017|title=Prey's Asian protagonist is refreshing in a sea of bearded white dudes|url=https://venturebeat.com/2017/03/12/preys-asian-protagonist-is-refreshing-in-a-sea-of-bearded-white-dudes/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313102126/http://venturebeat.com/2017/03/12/preys-asian-protagonist-is-refreshing-in-a-sea-of-bearded-white-dudes/|archive-date=March 13, 2017|access-date=October 23, 2020|website=VentureBeat|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Scaife|first=Steven|date=July 5, 2017|title=Prey Lets Me Be Asian|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/games/prey/prey-lets-me-be-asian/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803160117/https://www.pastemagazine.com/games/prey/prey-lets-me-be-asian/|archive-date=August 3, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020|website=pastemagazine.com|language=en}}</ref>

''[[PCGamesN]]'' reported that the Windows version of ''Prey'' lacked the technical problems of ''Dishonored 2'', calling it "the best performing [[AAA (video game industry)|triple-A]] game" they had seen in several months.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-pc-performance-graphics-tech-review | title = Prey PC graphics, performance and 4K analysis - the PCGamesN tech review | first = Matt | last = Perslow | date = May 4, 2017 | access-date = May 4, 2017 | work = [[PCGamesN]] | archive-date = September 28, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200928141849/https://www.pcgamesn.com/prey/prey-pc-performance-graphics-tech-review | url-status = live }}</ref> ''[[Eurogamer]]''{{'}}s Digital Foundry found the computer version of ''Prey'' to run exceedingly well across even low-end computers, in contrast to problems it saw for ''Dishonored 2'' at release.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/digitalfoundry-2017-prey-runs-beautifully-on-pc | title = Prey PC: even a budget rig can hit 1080p60 | first = David | last = Berton | date = May 11, 2017 | access-date = May 11, 2017 | work = [[Eurogamer]] | archive-date = December 23, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201223231024/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/digitalfoundry-2017-prey-runs-beautifully-on-pc | url-status = live }}</ref> However, some reviewers and players found that after several hours of playing on the computer version, their saved games would become corrupted, and the game would crash when transitioning between areas. Restoring from older saves would eventually cause those to be corrupted as well, making the game impossible to complete.<ref name="BugFixPromise">{{cite web | url = http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/05/09/prey-bethesda-aiming-to-have-a-patch-to-fix-game-breaking-bugs-this-week | title = Prey: Bethesda Aiming to Have a Patch to Fix Game-Breaking Bugs 'This Week' | first = Jonathan | last = Dornbrush | date = May 10, 2017 | access-date = May 11, 2017 | work = [[IGN]] | archive-date = May 10, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170510072659/http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/05/09/prey-bethesda-aiming-to-have-a-patch-to-fix-game-breaking-bugs-this-week | url-status = live }}</ref> Arkane deployed a patch to fix the problem on May 12.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dornbush |first1=Jonathon |title=Prey's Patch is Out of Beta, Fixes Game-Breaking Bugs on PC |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/05/12/preys-patch-is-out-of-beta-fixes-game-breaking-bugs-on-pc |website=[[IGN]] |publisher=[[Ziff Davis]] |access-date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512015009/https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/05/12/preys-patch-is-out-of-beta-fixes-game-breaking-bugs-on-pc |archive-date=May 12, 2017 |date=May 11, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The game's critical reception improved over time. Nic Reuben from ''Rock, Paper, Shotgun'' described ''Prey'' as its "masterpiece", adding that it was a smartly designed game exuberating with confidence and commending the countless gameplay possibilities provided within its systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/remembering-prey-arkane-austins-masterpiece|title=Remembering Prey, Arkane Austin’s masterpiece|first=Nic|last=Reuben|work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]|date=May 8, 2024|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=January 6, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106194529/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/remembering-prey-arkane-austins-masterpiece|url-status=live}}</ref> Cass Marshall from ''Polygon'' called the game "a testament to human imagination, and one of the best immersive sims ever made", praising its countless gameplay options and the presence of dynamic enemies such as the Nightmare for creating unique playthroughs for each player and providing replayability.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/gaming/24151555/prey-arkane-studios-austin-games-microsoft-xbox/|title=Prey, Arkane Austin’s masterpiece, still deserves your attention|first=Cass|last=Marshall|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=May 8, 2024|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=May 3, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503180907/https://www.polygon.com/gaming/24151555/prey-arkane-studios-austin-games-microsoft-xbox|url-status=live}}</ref> Robert Jones from ''[[PC Gamer]]'' wrote that the game was a "god-tier level" immersive sim, adding that the game "evokes the feeling of playing a spiritual sequel to ''[[Half-Life 2]]''".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fps/as-arkane-austin-falls-to-the-shareholders-its-masterpiece-prey-that-elevated-immersive-sims-to-a-god-tier-level-is-slashed-in-price-by-80/|title=As Arkane Austin falls to the shareholders, its masterpiece Prey, which 'elevated immersive sims to a god-tier level', is slashed in price by 80%|first=Robert|last=Jones|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=May 9, 2024|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=December 10, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251210092640/https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fps/as-arkane-austin-falls-to-the-shareholders-its-masterpiece-prey-that-elevated-immersive-sims-to-a-god-tier-level-is-slashed-in-price-by-80/|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''GamesRadar'', Rick Lane felt that ''Prey'' had exceeded its inspiration (''System Shock''). He added that ''Talos I'' was "the single finest example of 3D level design", while praising its story for its exploration of themes such as memory and identity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/arkanes-sci-fi-immersive-sim-prey-was-a-shock-to-the-system-for-players-and-its-developer-alike/|title=Arkane's sci-fi immersive sim Prey was a shock to the system, for players and its developer alike|first=Rick|last=Lane|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=January 2, 2024|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=December 12, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212115310/https://www.gamesradar.com/arkanes-sci-fi-immersive-sim-prey-was-a-shock-to-the-system-for-players-and-its-developer-alike/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Sales ===
''Prey'' debuted at No. 2 on the weekly sales charts in the United Kingdom, trailing the [[Nintendo Switch]] port of ''[[Mario Kart 8]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/mario-kart-8-deluxe-holds-off-prey-in-uk-game-chart|title=Mario Kart 8 Deluxe holds off Prey in UK game chart|first=Wesley|last=Yin-Poole|work=[[Eurogamer]]|date=May 8, 2017|accessdate=March 24, 2026}}</ref> These figures were considered disappointing due to a lack of competition from [[AAA (video game industry)|AAA]] new releases and the fact that the opening week sales were 60% down from Arkane's previous title, ''[[Dishonored 2]]''.<ref name="MCVSales">{{cite web |last=Byrne |first=Katharine |date=May 10, 2017 |url=https://www.mcvuk.com/prey-is-bethesdas-review-policy-really-to-blame/ |title=Prey: is Bethesda's review policy really to blame? |work=[[MCV (magazine)|MCV]] |publisher=[[NewBay Media]] |access-date=May 18, 2017 |archive-date=April 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408151329/https://www.mcvuk.com/prey-is-bethesdas-review-policy-really-to-blame/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Additionally, Bethesda's decision to hold review copies until the release date was mentioned by outlets as a factor for the weak launch.<ref name="MCVSales"/> ''Prey'' captured the top spot in its second week of release. In doing so, ''Prey'' became the first Bethesda game since 2016's ''[[Doom (2016 video game)|Doom]]'' to reach number one on the United Kingdom weekly sales charts.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hussain |first=Tamoor |date=May 15, 2017 |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/top-10-uk-sales-chart-prey-makes-it-to-no1-in-seco/1100-6450037/ |title=Top 10 UK Sales Chart: Prey Makes It To No.1 In Second Week |work=GameSpot |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=May 18, 2017 |archive-date=August 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820044425/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/top-10-uk-sales-chart-prey-makes-it-to-no1-in-seco/1100-6450037/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was the 5th best-selling game in the US in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/us-games-spending-fell-11-percent-on-weak-software-market-npd|title=US games spending fell 11% on weak software market - NPD|first=Matthew|last=Handrahan|work=[[Gameindustry.biz]]|date=June 20, 2017|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=February 14, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214120441/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/us-games-spending-fell-11-percent-on-weak-software-market-npd|url-status=live}}</ref> 

With both ''Prey'' and ''Dishonored 2'' underperforming commercially, Bethesda Softworks and Arkane Studios decided to pivot their strategy from making [[immersive sim]]s to [[live service]] games, resulting in the departure of Colantonio from Arkane and the release of ''[[Redfall]]'' in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/arkanes-founder-left-because-bethesda-did-not-want-to-do-the-kind-of-games-that-we-wanted-to-make-and-thats-how-it-ended-up-with-redfall/|title=Arkane's founder left because Bethesda 'did not want to do the kind of games that we wanted to make', and that's how it ended up with Redfall|first=Fraser|last=Brown|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=October 31, 2024|accessdate=February 19, 2026|archive-date=November 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113063522/https://www.pcgamer.com/games/arkanes-founder-left-because-bethesda-did-not-want-to-do-the-kind-of-games-that-we-wanted-to-make-and-thats-how-it-ended-up-with-redfall/|url-status=live}}</ref>
